chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Isma'il ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who swore to sever ties of kinship, so he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: There is no vow in disobedience, and no oath in severing ties of kinship.'
And I asked him about a man whom the ruler compelled to swear by divorce or other means, and he swore, so he said: 'There is no blame upon him.'
And I asked him about a man who fears for his wealth from the ruler, so he swears to save it from them, he said: 'There is no blame upon him.'
And I asked him: Does a man swear regarding his brother's wealth as he swears regarding his own wealth? He said: 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on an oath to sever kinship ties or an oath compelled by a ruler?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the jurisprudence of oaths, establishing that severing kinship ties (qat' al-rahim) invalidates the oath's binding nature, as 'no oath in disobedience' is valid. It further provides relief for those under political compulsion (ikrah) by rulers, ruling that such oaths incur no expiation (kaffarah), while also confirming that one may swear regarding another's property as one's own. This reflects the Shia principle of distinguishing between voluntary transgression and forced necessity in legal rulings.
